sentences.text: Eutreptornis, meaning "changing bird," is an extinct bird from the Late Eocene of Utah that may belong to the Cariamiformes group. The genus is known only from the type species Eutreptornis uintae, which is represented by a tibiotarsus and tarsometatarsus found in the Uinta Formation of Utah.
Eutreptornis holds the record for the smallest known bathornithid remains.
The genus Eutreptornis was described by Cracraft in 1971.
Eutreptornis was certainly a terrestrial predator, likely similar to its living relatives, the seriemas.
Eutreptornis lived alongside rich mammalian megafauna like Megacerops and other birds, including larger bathornithids and flightless geranoidids.
Eutreptornis belongs to the family Bathornithidae.
Fossils of Eutreptornis date to the Late Eocene epoch. Eutreptornis lived between 45.9 and 39.7 million years ago, during the Lutetian to Bartonian stages.
Although traditionally classified as a bathornithid, the incomplete fossil record and differences from other members have raised doubts about this affiliation.
